TermsMt.metaDescription: Terms of use of the Maltese pages of Apercura: a free, factual directory of community pharmacies in Malta and Gozo, without online booking.
TermsMt.title: Terms of use
TermsMt.lead: The rules for using the Maltese pages of Apercura, for the public and for pharmacies alike.

service.heading: The service
body: Apercura lists, free of charge, the community pharmacies on the Medicines Authority's register of licensed pharmacies in Malta and Gozo. It is a directory only: no appointment is booked and no medicine is sold through Apercura in Malta. It is run by the service provider named in the legal notice.
Using the directory requires no account. Using the site means accepting these terms.

content.heading: What the pages contain
body: Pages show factual information from the register, as it publishes it, in a neutral order, without ratings, reviews, advertising or paid placement. No pharmacy pays to be listed or to be shown first, and none is endorsed. They list pharmacies, never individual pharmacists, and name no medicine.

The information is as current as the register's last edition and may be incomplete or out of date: check it with the pharmacy before you go. Pages do not say which pharmacy is open on a Sunday or a public holiday: the official roster does. Every page says how to report an error.

health.heading: Not medical advice
body: Apercura gives no medical advice and is not an emergency service. In an emergency, call 112. A pharmacist can advise on minor illnesses; for anything else, see your doctor or a health centre.

facilities.heading: For pharmacies
body: Claiming a page is free. It requires a document proving that the claimant runs the pharmacy or acts for it, checked by a person before the page is handed over.

The holder of a page is responsible for the information they add. It must stay factual, accurate and up to date, must not advertise a medicine, a product or a service, and must respect the rules that bind pharmacists, among them the Pharmacy Council's Code of Ethics and the Medicinal Products (Advertising) Regulations (S.L. 458.32).

removal.heading: Correcting or removing a page
body: A fact taken from the register is corrected with the Medicines Authority, and the page follows at the next import; anything else can be reported with the form on the data page. Anyone a page is about can ask for it to be removed at any time: the data page explains how. A claimed page can only be removed by its holder.

liability.heading: Liability
body: The provider does its best to keep the service available and accurate, but cannot guarantee it. It is not responsible for the information pharmacies add to their pages. Nothing in these terms limits a liability that the law does not allow to be limited, such as liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence. These terms will be specified during the legal review.

ip.heading: Code and data
body: The source code is published under the AGPL-3.0 licence. Directory data is re-used under CC BY 4.0: the data page lists every source.

law.heading: Governing law and disputes
body: These terms are governed by French law, the law of the provider's establishment. If you use the site as a consumer living in Malta, you keep the protection of the mandatory rules of Maltese law and can bring a claim before the Maltese courts. In case of a dispute, first write to the contact address to look for an amicable solution.

AccessibilityMt.metaDescription: Accessibility of the Maltese pages of Apercura: the WCAG 2.2 AA target, what was checked, what remains, and how to report a problem.
AccessibilityMt.title: Accessibility
AccessibilityMt.lead: Apercura is designed for everyone, including older and low-vision people. This statement says where the Maltese pages stand.

scope.heading: Scope
body: This statement is voluntary. The Accessibility of the Websites and Mobile Applications of Public Sector Bodies Regulations (S.L. 418.03) bind public sector bodies, which Apercura is not, and the Accessibility Measures (European Accessibility Act) Regulations (S.L. 627.03) bind the products and services they list, which a free directory is not. Its provider nevertheless aims at the same standard on every page: WCAG 2.2 level AA.

status.heading: Where the site stands
body: The Maltese pages share the code of the other markets' pages and their tests. The site partially meets WCAG 2.2 AA: this rests on a self-assessment and automated tests, not yet on a full audit, which is in progress. The pages are in English only for now; a Maltese version is planned.

tests.heading: What was checked
list: Automated axe-core checks (WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 rules, levels A and AA) on every page type, at every release.
Keyboard-only journeys with a visible focus.
Body text of at least 18 px, targets of at least 44 px, nothing that relies on colour alone, no horizontal scrolling at 390 px.

pending.heading: What remains to be checked
list: A manual pass with the VoiceOver and NVDA screen readers.
A full audit against WCAG 2.2 AA on a sample of pages.

feedback.heading: Report a problem
body: If a page or a feature is hard to use, write to the address below: say which page and what blocked you. We answer within one month and, where needed, give you the information in another form.

DataMt.metaDescription: Where the Maltese pages of Apercura come from: the Medicines Authority's register of licensed pharmacies and the places of the Planning Authority, the NSO and the Address Registrar, with their licence, what is not imported, and how to correct or remove a page.
DataMt.title: Data and sources
DataMt.lead: Every Maltese page is built from the Medicines Authority's register of licensed pharmacies, published as open data. Here is where it comes from, under which licence and attribution, what is left out and why, and how to correct or remove a page.

status.heading: Last update
status.body: The Medicines Authority updates its register on the national open data portal when a licence is granted, moved or revoked. The directory reads it every week and imports it when it has changed; a page changes only when its facts change in the register.
status.notImported: The Maltese directory has not been imported yet on this site.

sources.heading: Sources
sources.body: Every source is published under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence (CC BY 4.0), which asks for the source to be credited. Each attribution below is printed word for word, and every Maltese page prints those of its sources.
sources.caption: Data sources of the Maltese directory

mt-pharmacies.use: Community pharmacies: names as licensed, licence numbers, addresses, localities, postcodes, phone numbers and points
mt-pharmacies.frequency: When a licence changes, by the Medicines Authority

mt-local-councils.use: The boundaries of the 68 localities (local councils), in which every pharmacy is placed, and the point of each locality

mt-localities.use: The six districts and two regions the localities belong to, and the localities' names in English and Maltese

map.name: Map data
map.use: The base map of the pages

conditions: The Medicines Authority publishes its register of licensed pharmacies on data.gov.mt under CC BY 4.0, which allows re-use, commercial or not, provided the source is credited and changes are indicated. Apercura reads that dataset, not the Authority's website, whose terms forbid the commercial reproduction of the website's own content.

The rules on advertising bind those who advertise: the Medicinal Products (Advertising) Regulations (S.L. 458.32) govern the advertising of medicines, and the Pharmacy Council's Code of Ethics limits pharmacists' self-advertising. Apercura names no medicine, and lists every licensed community pharmacy the same way, free, in a neutral order, without ranking or paid placement: a pharmacy that claims its page must keep what it adds factual and within those rules.
sources.termsText: The dataset on the European data portal

coverage.heading: Pharmacies covered
body: A page is a pharmacy, never a person. Malta's pages list:

kinds.MT_PHARMACY: Community pharmacies: every pharmacy of the Medicines Authority's register that serves the public, in Malta and Gozo

excluded.heading: What is not imported, and why
body: Some data would complete the directory but is not open, serves no member of the public, or names people:
list: The register's other pharmacies: the in-patient pharmacies of hospitals, the pharmacies of government entities (health centres, the Armed Forces, Sedqa), medical-oxygen dispensaries and a parenteral-nutrition dispensary. None serves the public at a counter.
Hospitals and health centres: no open list of Malta's state hospitals and health centres was found.

Doctors and dentists: the Medical Council lists its registers on the national catalogue, but publishes them as a search and in documents, and their republication waits for its written confirmation. No person is listed.
OpenStreetMap: used for the base map only, never as a source of pharmacies or of their positions, since its Open Database Licence (ODbL) is share-alike.
Data about individuals, never: no register of people, no ratings, no reviews.

unread.heading: Fields never read
body: The register publishes only what a pharmacy's page needs: its type, licence number, name, address, locality, postcode, phone and point. It names no licence holder or pharmacist, and the import reads nothing else.
list: The register's internal row number, which identifies nothing outside it.

locations.heading: Locations
body: Every pharmacy is shown at the point the register gives it, and placed in the locality whose boundary, from the Planning Authority, holds that point. A pharmacy without a point is placed in the locality its address names, at the locality's point: no pin marks it on a map, and its distance is approximate.

Localities are grouped in the six districts and two regions (Malta, and Gozo and Comino) of the National Statistics Office; their Maltese names are those of the Office of the Address Registrar's list of local councils.

identifiers.heading: Identifiers
body: The address of every page ends with the number of the pharmacy's licence, so that a page can be found and checked against the register:
list: /mt/facility/example-pharmacy-dl001: the pharmacy whose licence is DL 001, after dl.

correct.heading: Correct an error
body: The pages repeat the register: a lasting correction is made at the source, and the page follows at the next import after the corrected register is published.
For anything else, use the form: we check every report.
list: A pharmacy's name, address or phone: the licence holder tells the Medicines Authority, which keeps the register.
Website and opening hours: the register gives none; a pharmacy adds them by claiming its page.
correct.formBody: Give the address of the page and what is wrong.

remove.heading: Remove a page
body: Anyone a page is about can object to its publication at any time, without giving a reason (GDPR article 21). An unclaimed page is hidden as soon as the request arrives and deleted after a light check; it never comes back with the imports of the register. A claimed page is removed by its holder, from their space. Every page also has its own removal form.
remove.formTitle: Ask for a page to be removed
remove.formBody: Give the address of the page and an email address where we can answer you.
